newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics Q2 beats expectations.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics Q2 beats expectations.

text.p: U.S. Robotics' fiscal second quarter results beat expectations, boosted by strong sales of its new high-speed computer modem technology, analysts said Wednesday.
"It's an extremely strong quarter," Volpe, Welty & Co analyst Amar Senan said. "There was very good revenue growth, and the x2 products are being extermely well received in the marketplace."
After the market closed Wednesday, U.S. Robotics reported earnings for its second quarter ended March 31 of $0.77 a share excluding a one-time gain versus $0.55 last year.
According to First Call, the consensus estimate was $0.75 a share.
Revenues rose to $690.18 million from $454.51 last year.
In after hours trade, U.S. Robotics shares were up at 48 one from Wednesday's close of 47.
"It looks like they won the battle in the analog modem market," Senan said.
In February, U.S. Robotics began shipping its x2 desktop modems, followed in March by the hub technology, used by Internet Service Providers, for example.
The x2 technology allows users to download information from the Internet at speeds up to 56 kilobits per second or roughly twice as fast as today's standard analog modems.
There is no standard 56-K technology, so modem users must connect to an x2 modem or hub to get the higher speeds.

Analysts noted the days of sales outstanding (DSO), which measures how long it takes a company to collect receivables, had increased in second quarter to 95 days from 88 in the first, but that was to be expected because of the new product release late in the quarter and an increase in international sales.
"The only negative anyone could derive is DSO, and I certainly hope they look beyond that," said Therese Murphy, an analyst with Smith Barney.
U.S. Robotics said it expects its merger with 3Com Corp to close in June, and the company does not expect to report separate earnings for its fiscal third quarter.
